items.answer: In: src/indicators/daysWithDelay.mjs and delayCount.mjs (option lists + WL functions) and their tests. Out: Indicator 1 and its collapsing of 2-3 (C3), any UI/dropdown rendering (C4), counting delays in 12 months (C6), aggregation to an overall rating.

Yes: each requirement has WL mapping per option; C1/C2/C5 give exact strings, trimming and error behaviour, so G/W/T with concrete values can be written for every option and for invalid input (e.g. '>3 Days', '>3  days', null, 3).

One textual mismatch: REQ-03-02 shows the option as '≤3 days' (Unicode) whereas C1 fixes the string as '<=3 days' (ASCII). Resolved explicitly by C1, which is the business-confirmed clarification: only '<=3 days' is valid; '≤3 days' throws RangeError. REQ-03-03 gives no WL for '0' and REQ-03-02 none for 'no delay'/'<=3 days'; C2 resolves them to 0. No other conflicts.

items.answer: daysWithDelay.mjs: export const DAYS_WITH_DELAY_OPTIONS = ['no delay','<=3 days','>3 days','>60 days','>90 days'] (ordered) and daysWithDelayWl(option) -> 0|0|2|3|4. delayCount.mjs: export const DELAY_COUNT_OPTIONS = ['0','1','>1'] and delayCountWl(option) -> 0|1|2. Input: string, trimmed with String.prototype.trim(), exact case-sensitive match, inner whitespace untouched. Output: integer WL.

Any value not in the list after trim (wrong case, inner whitespace, empty string, whitespace-only, unknown text, '≤3 days') and any non-string (null, undefined, number, object, array) throws RangeError. No fallback WL.
Nothing exists yet (src/ and test/ are empty), so no backward-compatibility burden; no versioning. Exported option arrays are part of the contract for later screens.

items.question: Should the exported *_OPTIONS arrays be frozen (Object.freeze) or plain arrays? The contract says only 'the N strings, in order'.
options: Frozen arrays (safe against caller mutation; tests may assert Object.isFrozen)
Plain arrays (simplest; screens could mutate shared state)
items.impact: Internal robustness only; no change to values, order or WL mapping.

items.answer: Complete mapping: Ind.2 'no delay'->0, '<=3 days'->0, '>3 days'->2, '>60 days'->3, '>90 days'->4; Ind.3 '0'->0, '1'->1, '>1'->2. Options are mutually exclusive selections picked by the caller (not cumulative ranges), so no bucketing of numeric days is done here.
The '≤' character is not an accepted alias; only ASCII '<=3 days' is valid per C1 (exact match, C5). QA should include '≤3 days' as a RangeError case.
